title: data:// URLs being considered as IsSecureContext
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Consider the following HTML:

```html
<body></body>
<script>
    window.onload = () => {
        const iframeHTML = `
<!DOCTYPE html>
<script>
console.log(isSecureContext);
<\/script>`;

        console.log(isSecureContext);
        const frame = document.createElement("iframe");
        frame.src = "data:text/html;charset=utf-8," + encodeURIComponent(iframeHTML);
        document.body.appendChild(frame);
    }
</script>
```

This gives:

- Chromium: True, False
- Webkit: True, False
- Gecko: True, True


Per spec, this should log true in all cases (like Gecko) since [secure context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#secure-context) operates on the top level creation URL which means that the result should be true and true.


However, what makes all engines inconsistent with the spec is that if the data URL of the iframe:

```
data:text/html;charset=utf-8,%0A%3C!DOCTYPE%20html%3E%0A%3Cscript%3E%0Aconsole.log(isSecureContext)%3B%0A%3C%2Fscript%3E
```

Is run directly, all browsers will log false. Per spec, I believe this should be true, since top level URL is a data URL, and [secure context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#secure-context) uses is [URL potentially trustworthy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-secure-contexts/#potentially-trustworthy-url), which returns potentially trustworthy for data:// URLs explicitly. 

So I am left unsure about both what the behaviour of data scheme URLs should be, and whether the top level creation URL is the URL that should be used.

The top level url part seems to relate to https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6369 where we should perhaps not be using top level URL, however it seems like all browsers are consistent in not considering data URLs as isSecureContext, which seems like a good first alignment of the spec with implementations whether or not top level URL is used.
